findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 2026 release (8-K, 2026-10-20) reports North America revenue $2,160M, down 5% sequentially from $2,276M, 'primarily driven by lower pressure pumping services in U.S. Land', and Completion & Production revenue -4% q/q on 'lower stimulation activity in the Western Hemisphere'; LBRT is a pure-play U.S./Canada frac provider whose Q2 ran ~40 active fleets at record utilization with revenue $1.19B, so the largest frac peer's print points to flat-to-lower LBRT Q3 frac revenue, while consensus adj. EPS ($0.03-0.07) already sits below Q2's $0.09.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue consensus by ~9% ($1.19B vs $1.09B) and EPS by a cent and the stock fell 21.96% (baseline); this name has not paid for reported-quarter beats, so a modest miss on the quarter is likely also a small driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: LBRT fell 3.0% on 10-20 (17.09 -> 16.58), the day HAL printed, and ProPetro (PUMP) slid from 9.27 on 10-02 to 7.565 on 10-21; the consensus already embeds a sequential decline. If it were fully priced the street EPS would sit at or below zero, not $0.03-0.07, and LBRT's management would not be writing 'improving completions cycle' on 10-20.
findings.independence: Proxy from a peer, not LBRT's own number. ProPetro's tape (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PUMP?range=1mo&interval=1d) points the same way; LBRT's own 10-20 dividend release points the other way (filed separately).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-20, the day before the print, Liberty raised its quarterly dividend 11% from $0.09 to $0.10 (payable 2026-12-18), with CEO Ron Gusek citing 'an improving completions cycle and the strong momentum across our power initiatives'; a board raising the payout while carrying ~$1.3B of convertibles and heavy power capex is a management read of the Q4/2027 outlook it will present on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last raise (13%, announced 2025-10-14) preceded the Q3 2025 print that moved +28.31% (baseline); one observation, and that move had other drivers.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise is on the wire, but the stock fell 3% that day on HAL's print, so the market weighed the peer's weak U.S. land read above the company's own forward signal; if the signal were priced the stock would not be 12% below where it was a week earlier while the sector index is flat.
findings.independence: Same company document as no other finding. Oil (separate finding) is supportive of the 'improving cycle' claim; HAL's release contradicts it for Q3 but speaks to the past quarter, not the outlook.

findings.finding: WTI front-month traded ~$97-101 through October 2026 (weekly closes 91.85 on 10-05, 101.41 on 10-12, 101.79 on 10-19, 97.01 intraday 10-21) against $78-87 in August, so the Q3 call, which in October usually carries Liberty's first view on next-year completions, lands into the strongest oil tape of the year; Halliburton's own 2027 outlook 'assumes a flat North America market' and calls a frac recovery 'purely upside'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (the last October print with a next-year read) moved +28.31%; Q4 2025 +16.24%. Guidance-bearing prints have produced the largest moves in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: OIH is flat over the month while LBRT is -12% since 10-13, so LBRT is trading off power sentiment and the U.S. land Q3 read rather than the oil price; if a constructive 2027 completions view were priced, LBRT would have tracked the oil-service group rather than diverged from it. Macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company, hence small.
findings.independence: HAL 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/45012/000004501226000070/livemastererdocument.htm) frames NA frac recovery as upside; LBRT's 10-20 dividend release cites an 'improving completions cycle'. Both are separate from the price series.

findings.finding: LBRT's 12% drop from 10-13 to 10-20 coincided with a power/data-center sell-off visible in its closest listed power comparable, Solaris Energy Infrastructure (SEI: 77.83 on 10-13 to 63.34 on 10-20, -19%); SEI rebounded +9.7% to 69.46 intraday on 10-21 while LBRT rose only ~1.4% (16.58 -> 16.81), so a power update on the call (PowerBridge 300+ MW targeted late 2027, SLB alliance, Bergen/Wartsila/Jenbacher equipment orders) lands on a name that has not joined the sector's rebound.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print that announced the PowerBridge JV alongside Q2 moved -21.96%, so power announcements alone have not been rewarded; the October 2025 print (+28.31%) came with a power-heavy narrative.
findings.why_not_priced: If the power drawdown were being unwound for LBRT as for SEI, LBRT would be up several percent today rather than ~1.4%. A lagged catch-up is a mechanism only if the call gives a power datum; inference, sized small.
findings.independence: LBRT price series (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LBRT?range=1mo&interval=1d) and Q2 release power disclosures (https://investors.libertyenergy.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2026/07-22-2026-231109602). Both price series are Yahoo, one source type.
